addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Integration Open Items — Consolidated
2	
3	Open items requiring client confirmation across the fifteen external integrations in scope for the Zimmermann PWA storefront. Each item is a decision, contract, credential, or sign-off that must land before the corresponding integration can be implemented end-to-end against a real account.
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	We need their documentations or implementation guide for at least:
8	Omneo iframe (for communication preferences), Booxi, MuleSoft (for GiveX balance check, order history/detail, returns).
9	
10	Then for all the external systems (also incl. Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize) we'll need their relevant Zimmermann-specific IDs, for each environment (dev/uat/prod etc) if applicable, and their associated Didomi feature/vendor ID if consent-gated.
11	
12	Plus:
13	- GiveX: Do we need reCAPTCHA for balance check?
14	- CAI-023 Can MuleSoft aggregate stock?
15	
16	| # | Integration | Items |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| 1 | SFCC | 2 |
19	| 2 | Contentful | 3 |
20	| 3 | MuleSoft | 4 |
21	| 4 | Omneo | 3 (all hard blockers) |
22	| 5 | GiveX | 3 |
23	| 6 | Booxi | 4 (scope/timeline TBC) |
24	| 7 | Adyen | 2 |
25	| 8 | Global-e | 2 |
26	| 9 | Google Maps | 1 |
27	| 10 | reCAPTCHA | 2 |
28	| 11 | Narvar | 2 |
29	| 12 | Didomi | 2 |
30	| 13 | GTM | 2 |
31	| 14 | Inside Chat | 0 |
32	| 15 | Optimizely | 1 |
33	| 16 | Crazy Egg | 3 |
34	| 17 | Measmerize | 2 |
35	| 18 | Vimeo | 2 |
36	
37	Total: 40 items across 18 integrations.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 1. SFCC
42	
43	1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.
44	
45	2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) assumes `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to a different origin than the SCAPI host (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). If they share an origin the two pools should be merged.
46	
47	## 2. Contentful
48	
49	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all seven storefronts.
50	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
51	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.
52	
53	## 3. MuleSoft
54	
55	1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
56	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
57	3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
58	4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).
59	
60	## 4. Omneo
61	
62	No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.
63	
64	1. **Communication Preferences iFrame — confirm the non-Shopify auth handshake.** CRM-174 confirms the screen is rendered as an Omneo iFrame; the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection (location, state, and language preference), and three clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is an enhancement, not in scope for launch). Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. However, Omneo's documented embed is a Shopify theme extension that authenticates via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy, which a PWA does not have. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: the Profile Portal embed URL, how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it, and the auth handshake outside Shopify (a customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach, or a server-minted customer-scoped token). If no embed path is available, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
65	2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:
66	   - Omneo tenant / account identifier (the value that appears in the embed URL, e.g. the account subdomain or path slug)
67	   - Exact embed URL host(s) and path(s) for the Communication Preferences widget — needed both to build the iFrame and to add to the storefront's `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` allowlist
68	   - Any other public identifier the widget requires (widget ID, environment ID, configuration key)
69	3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.
70	
71	## 5. GiveX
72	
73	1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** The integration team to publish the request and response schema for the MuleSoft balance-check endpoint (`POST /givex/balance` placeholder) — the request carries both the card number and the PIN (secure PINs are enabled) — plus the error taxonomy that maps GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, including the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
74	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
75	3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.
76	
77	## 6. Booxi
78	
79	Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.
80	
81	1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
82	2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
83	3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
84	4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.
85	
86	## 7. Adyen
87	
88	1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
89	2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.
90	## 8. Global-e
91	
92	1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.
93	
94	2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.
95	
96	## 9. Google Maps
97	
98	1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
99	
100	## 10. reCAPTCHA
101	
102	1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
103	
104	2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.
105	
106	## 11. Narvar
107	
108	1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.
109	
110	2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.
111	
112	## 12. Didomi
113	
114	1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
115	2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.
116	
117	## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)
118	
119	1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
120	2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.
121	
122	## 14. Inside Chat
123	
124	No open items — PWA has zero Inside-Chat work.
125	
126	## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)
127	
128	Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.
129	
130	1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.
131	
132	## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)
133	
134	Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).
135	
136	1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
137	2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
138	3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.
139	
140	## 17. Measmerize
141	
142	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
143	2. **Brand code UUIDs.** Script URL (`https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`) and product identifier (SFCC SKU, `data-product-code`) are confirmed from vendor docs. Measmerize issues exactly two brand codes per retailer: one for production and one shared across all non-production environments (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT). Measmerize to supply both values to be set as MRT environment variables. **Owner:** Zimmermann / Measmerize.
144	
145	## 18. Vimeo
146	
147	Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.
148	
149	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
150	
151	2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## Summary

Omneo iframe (for communication preferences), Booxi, MuleSoft (for GiveX balance check, order history/detail, returns).

Then for all the external systems (also incl. Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize) we'll need their relevant Zimmermann-specific IDs, for each environment (dev/uat/prod etc) if applicable, and their associated Didomi feature/vendor ID if consent-gated.

Plus:
- GiveX: Do we need reCAPTCHA for balance check?
- CAI-023 Can MuleSoft aggregate stock?

| # | Integration | Items |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SFCC | 2 |
| 2 | Contentful | 3 |
| 3 | MuleSoft | 4 |

| 16 | Crazy Egg | 3 |
| 17 | Measmerize | 2 |
| 18 | Vimeo | 2 |

Total: 40 items across 18 integrations.

---

## 1. SFCC

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) assumes `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to a different origin than the SCAPI host (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). If they share an origin the two pools should be merged.

## 2. Contentful

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all seven storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.

## 3. MuleSoft

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).

## 4. Omneo

No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.

1. **Communication Preferences iFrame — confirm the non-Shopify auth handshake.** CRM-174 confirms the screen is rendered as an Omneo iFrame; the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection (location, state, and language preference), and three clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is an enhancement, not in scope for launch). Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. However, Omneo's documented embed is a Shopify theme extension that authenticates via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy, which a PWA does not have. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: the Profile Portal embed URL, how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it, and the auth handshake outside Shopify (a customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach, or a server-minted customer-scoped token). If no embed path is available, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:
   - Omneo tenant / account identifier (the value that appears in the embed URL, e.g. the account subdomain or path slug)
   - Exact embed URL host(s) and path(s) for the Communication Preferences widget — needed both to build the iFrame and to add to the storefront's `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` allowlist
   - Any other public identifier the widget requires (widget ID, environment ID, configuration key)
3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

## 5. GiveX

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** The integration team to publish the request and response schema for the MuleSoft balance-check endpoint (`POST /givex/balance` placeholder) — the request carries both the card number and the PIN (secure PINs are enabled) — plus the error taxonomy that maps GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, including the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 6. Booxi

Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.

1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

## 7. Adyen

1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.
## 8. Global-e

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

## 9. Google Maps

1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

## 10. reCAPTCHA

1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 11. Narvar

1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.

2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.

## 12. Didomi

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.

## 14. Inside Chat

No open items — PWA has zero Inside-Chat work.

## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)

Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.

1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)

Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).

1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 17. Measmerize

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Brand code UUIDs.** Script URL (`https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`) and product identifier (SFCC SKU, `data-product-code`) are confirmed from vendor docs. Measmerize issues exactly two brand codes per retailer: one for production and one shared across all non-production environments (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT). Measmerize to supply both values to be set as MRT environment variables. **Owner:** Zimmermann / Measmerize.

## 18. Vimeo

Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

6	
7	## 1. Problem
8	
9	Salesforce PWA Kit ships a fully functioning reference storefront (`@salesforce/retail-react-app`). 10

12

22

When the bundler resolves a file, it checks `overrides/` first. If a matching file exists there, it uses that. Otherwise, the base package version is used. This is Salesforce's own recommended customisation model for PWA Kit.
24	
25	In practice, this means:
26	
27	- We only create a file in `overrides/` when we actually need to change something. Everything else runs as-is from the base package.
28	- Brand-new Zimmermann components that have no equivalent in the base package live in a dedicated `custom/` folder inside `overrides/app/components/`. This keeps Zimmermann-authored components visually separate from base-template overrides.
29	- All files in `overrides/` will be TypeScript (`.ts` / `.tsx`), even when the original base file is JavaScript. We pick TypeScript to make the code more reliable, easier to debug, and more robust to maintain over time.
30	
31	### The upgrade contract
32	
33	Upgrading to a new version of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` means bumping the dependency version and reconciling only the files we have actually overridden. The fewer files in `overrides/`, the easier the upgrade will be.
34	
35	**Working principle:** Stay close to the base template. Visual changes go through Chakra UI theme tokens. Structural changes (deviation from the base template's data flow, routing, or layout) should be reviewed against upgrade impact before being merged.
36	
37	Before copying a base file into `overrides/`, we should confirm that the change cannot be achieved through configuration or a Chakra UI theme token instead. For example, changing a button's border-radius via the theme is better than overriding the entire Button component. The rule is: Prefer configuration over override.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 3. Server-Side vs Client-Side Rendering
42	
43	PWA Kit always runs the server-side rendering (SSR) pipeline — every page produces server-rendered HTML. The decision for each page type is what data is rendered on the server versus fetched by the browser after the page loads.
44	
45	| Page type | Approach | Reason |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Product pages, category pages, content pages, boutique pages, homepages | Full SSR — all content and data is rendered on the server | Must be indexable by search engines. LCP-critical. |
48	| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | SSR shell + client-side data — the server renders the page frame (header, footer, loading skeleton); personalised data loads in the browser after hydration | Personalised data cannot be edge-cached and has no SEO value. These pages are blocked in `robots.txt`. |
49	| Search results, filtered category pages | SSR shell + client-side data | Filter and sort state is driven by the user in the browser. Blocked in `robots.txt`. |
50	
51	"SSR shell + client-side data" still gives users an instant first paint of the page frame. No page is purely client-rendered.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 4. Performance and Third-Party Scripts
56	
57	**The constraint:** LCP ≤ 2 s at mobile p75. Third-party scripts are the primary risk to hitting this target.
58	
59	**Our rule:** Nothing that is not required for the first paint loads during the critical rendering path. This applies to all analytics, marketing, tracking, and support scripts.
60	
61	### How this is enforced
62	
63	All third-party scripts that require user consent are loaded via the Didomi consent callback. They do not load at all until consent is granted, and they are deferred or injected after the page has hydrated — so they never block the first paint.
64	
65	reCAPTCHA is loaded only when the user interacts with a registration or login form. It is not present on any other page.
66	
67	### One exception: Optimizely Web (US storefront only)
68	
69	Optimizely Web must run *before* the page renders to prevent A/B test flicker. It is injected directly into the page `<head>` as a script tag — intentionally on the critical path — and scoped only to the US storefront. This is the agreed trade-off for A/B testing capability.
70	
71	It is still consent-gated: Optimizely does not activate experiments until Didomi consent is granted. On a user's first visit (before consent is given), Optimizely is dormant, so there will be no flicker. The anti-flicker benefit applies from the second visit onwards, once consent has been stored and Optimizely activates on page load.
72	
73	### Images
74	
75	- All product and editorial images are served from Contentful, not from SFCC.
76	- The PWA generates `srcset` and `sizes` attributes per breakpoint, using AVIF as the primary format with WebP and JPEG as fallbacks.
77	- The hero image (the LCP candidate) is priority-loaded. All other images are lazy-loaded.
78	- Images are not served at a higher resolution than their display size warrants. The `srcset` and `sizes` attributes tell the browser which resolution to fetch at each breakpoint — a thumbnail slot will not download a full-resolution image.
79	
80	### Video
81	
82	- Product videos are hosted on Vimeo. They are displayed behind a facade — a poster image with a play button. The Vimeo player JavaScript does not load until the user interacts with the video, so it never lands on the LCP critical path.
83	- Editorial page videos are managed in Contentful by default. They can also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## 5. Consent Gating
88	
89	Didomi is the consent management platform. It controls whether third-party scripts are allowed to load.
90	
91	**Default rule:** if consent state cannot be determined, no third-party scripts load. The system fails closed — no scripts, no tracking.
92

95	- GTM and everything it loads (GA4, Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Inside Chat)

# Technical Solution Design — Frontend

*Draft. Last updated 2026-06-17. Scope: how the Zimmermann storefront customises PWA Kit, how pages are rendered, and how performance and consent are managed on the client side.*

---

## 1. Problem

Salesforce PWA Kit ships a fully functioning reference storefront (`@salesforce/retail-react-app`). We need to customise it for Zimmermann — visually, behaviourally, and for integrations — without forking it. Forking would mean owning all future upgrades ourselves, which is expensive. We choose an approach that keeps upgrades quick and easy.

We also need to balance these competing concerns on every page:

- **SEO and performance:** Pages must be server-rendered and fast, with LCP ≤ 2 s at mobile p75
- **Personalisation:** Cart, account, and order data is unique per-customer and cannot be cached on edge
- **Consent:** Third-party analytics and marketing scripts must not load until the user consents

---

## 2. Customisation Model: The Overrides Pattern

### How it works

We do not fork the base package. Instead, we maintain an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`. When the bundler resolves a file, it checks `overrides/` first. If a matching file exists there, it uses that. Otherwise, the base package version is used. This is Salesforce's own recommended customisation model for PWA Kit.

In practice, this means:

- We only create a file in `overrides/` when we actually need to change something. Everything else runs as-is from the base package.
- Brand-new Zimmermann components that have no equivalent in the base package live in a dedicated `custom/` folder inside `overrides/app/components/`. This keeps Zimmermann-authored components visually separate from base-template overrides.
- All files in `overrides/` will be TypeScript (`.ts` / `.tsx`), even when the original base file is JavaScript. We pick TypeScript to make the code more reliable, easier to debug, and more robust to maintain over time.

### The upgrade contract

Upgrading to a new version of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` means bumping the dependency version and reconciling only the files we have actually overridden. The fewer files in `overrides/`, the easier the upgrade will be.

**Working principle:** Stay close to the base template. Visual changes go through Chakra UI theme tokens. Structural changes (deviation from the base template's data flow, routing, or layout) should be reviewed against upgrade impact before being merged.

Before copying a base file into `overrides/`, we should confirm that the change cannot be achieved through configuration or a Chakra UI theme token instead. For example, changing a button's border-radius via the theme is better than overriding the entire Button component. The rule is: Prefer configuration over override.

---

## 3. Server-Side vs Client-Side Rendering

PWA Kit always runs the server-side rendering (SSR) pipeline — every page produces server-rendered HTML. The decision for each page type is what data is rendered on the server versus fetched by the browser after the page loads.

| Page type | Approach | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Product pages, category pages, content pages, boutique pages, homepages | Full SSR — all content and data is rendered on the server | Must be indexable by search engines. LCP-critical. |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | SSR shell + client-side data — the server renders the page frame (header, footer, loading skeleton); personalised data loads in the browser after hydration | Personalised data cannot be edge-cached and has no SEO value. These pages are blocked in `robots.txt`. |
| Search results, filtered category pages | SSR shell + client-side data | Filter and sort state is driven by the user in the browser. Blocked in `robots.txt`. |

"SSR shell + client-side data" still gives users an instant first paint of the page frame. No page is purely client-rendered.

---

## 4. Performance and Third-Party Scripts

**The constraint:** LCP ≤ 2 s at mobile p75. Third-party scripts are the primary risk to hitting this target.

**Our rule:** Nothing that is not required for the first paint loads during the critical rendering path. This applies to all analytics, marketing, tracking, and support scripts.

### How this is enforced

All third-party scripts that require user consent are loaded via the Didomi consent callback. They do not load at all until consent is granted, and they are deferred or injected after the page has hydrated — so they never block the first paint.

reCAPTCHA is loaded only when the user interacts with a registration or login form. It is not present on any other page.

### One exception: Optimizely Web (US storefront only)

Optimizely Web must run *before* the page renders to prevent A/B test flicker. It is injected directly into the page `<head>` as a script tag — intentionally on the critical path — and scoped only to the US storefront. This is the agreed trade-off for A/B testing capability.

It is still consent-gated: Optimizely does not activate experiments until Didomi consent is granted. On a user's first visit (before consent is given), Optimizely is dormant, so there will be no flicker. The anti-flicker benefit applies from the second visit onwards, once consent has been stored and Optimizely activates on page load.

### Images

- All product and editorial images are served from Contentful, not from SFCC.
- The PWA generates `srcset` and `sizes` attributes per breakpoint, using AVIF as the primary format with WebP and JPEG as fallbacks.
- The hero image (the LCP candidate) is priority-loaded. All other images are lazy-loaded.
- Images are not served at a higher resolution than their display size warrants. The `srcset` and `sizes` attributes tell the browser which resolution to fetch at each breakpoint — a thumbnail slot will not download a full-resolution image.

### Video

- Product videos are hosted on Vimeo. They are displayed behind a facade — a poster image with a play button. The Vimeo player JavaScript does not load until the user interacts with the video, so it never lands on the LCP critical path.
- Editorial page videos are managed in Contentful by default. They can also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred.

---

## 5. Consent Gating

Didomi is the consent management platform. It controls whether third-party scripts are allowed to load.

**Default rule:** if consent state cannot be determined, no third-party scripts load. The system fails closed — no scripts, no tracking.

### What is gated behind consent

- GTM and everything it loads (GA4, Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Inside Chat)
- Optimizely Web (US only) and Crazy Egg — these are loaded as direct page tags, not through GTM, but are still gated
- Narvar EDD widget

### What is not gated

reCAPTCHA is classified as strictly necessary (a security control, not analytics). However, in the EU and UK it is consent-gated anyway — the accepted consequence is that there is no bot protection on registration and login forms in those regions for sessions where the bot declines or ignores consent.

### Per-storefront consent defaults

Consent defaults differ by region and are specified in the functional requirements.

Each storefront has a unique Didomi notice ID. Consent preferences are stored in the browser for that notice ID — so AU preferences and UK preferences are completely separate records and cannot affect each other.

1	# Technical Solution Design — Zimmermann SFCC PWA (Architecture)
2	
3	*Draft for client sign-off. Last updated 2026-06-26. Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Purpose & Scope
8	
9	This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.
10	
11	**In scope:**
12	- Stack and build pipeline
13	- The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
14	- Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 7 storefronts in 6 regions
15	- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
16	- SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
17	- Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
18	- Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
19	- Open decisions requiring client input before build
20	
21	**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 2. Solution Overview
26	
27	A single PWA Kit codebase serves 7 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. 129	## 4. Customisation Model
130	
131	All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.
132	
133	**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.
134	
135	**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) live in a dedicated `custom/` folder under `overrides/app/components/`, separating Zimmermann-authored components from base-template overrides at a glance.
136

The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. 162	- Real values live only in the local, untracked environment file; only a template — variable names, no secret values — is committed to source control.

171	### 5.1 Storefronts

186	### 5.2 Entry routing
187	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
188	- **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
189	- **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.
190	
191	### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale
192	Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.
193	
194	### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed
195	- **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
196	- **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
197	- **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
198	- **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.
199	
200	### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts
201	All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):
202	
203	- **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
204	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
205	- **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
206	- **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

211	
212	Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.

221	## 7. Integration Map
222	
223	### 7.1 Classification model
224	Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.
225	
226	- **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
227	- **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
228	- **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
229	- **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
230	- **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).
231	
232	A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.
233	
234	> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

290	## 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
291	
292	### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)
293	All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.
294	
295	#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type
296	PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.
297	
298	| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
299	|---|---|---|
300	| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |
301	| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
302	| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |
303	
304	The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.
305	
306	### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang
307	Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.
308	
309	### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots
310	Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.
311	
312	### 8.4 Structured data
313	Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:
314	- **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
315	- **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
316	- **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
317	- **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).
318	
319	### 8.5 URL strategy
320	- Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
321	- Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
322	- 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.
323	
324	### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)
325	No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

329	## 9. Performance Strategy
330	
331	LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.
332	
333	| Metric | Target |
334	|---|---|
335	| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
336	| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
337	| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
338	| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |
339	
340	### 9.1 Third-party defer rule
341	Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags including the Inside Chat widget, via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.
342	
343	### 9.2 Other levers
344	- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
345	- **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
346	  - **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
347	  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
348	  - Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
349	- Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
350	- Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.
351	
352	### 9.3 Where performance is measured
353	The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.
354	
355	> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

411	## 12. Graceful Degradation
412	
413	Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.
414	
415	| System | Failure mode |
416	|---|---|
417	| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
418	| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |
419	| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |
420	| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
421	| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
422	| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
423	| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
424	| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |
425	
426	### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment
427	
428	The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.
429	
430	#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)
431	
432	- **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
433	- **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.
434	
435	#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)
436	
437	`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
438	
439	> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.
440	
441	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
442	
443	| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
444	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
445	| `sfcc-scapi` | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
446	| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
447	| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
448	| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com` | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
449	| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com` | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
450	| `google-places` | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
451	| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD — confirm with Integration team) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |
452	
453	**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).
