457	## 13. Testing Strategy
458	
459	Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.
460	
461	| Layer | Tool | Covers |
462	|---|---|---|
463	| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
464	| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |
465	| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |
466	
467	### 13.1 What is tested
468	Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.
469	
470	### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow
471	Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.
472	
473	### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures
474	E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 7 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)
475	
476	### 13.4 Selector priority
477	Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.

483	This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.
484	
485	### 14.1 Topology
486	
487	A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
488	
489	| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
490	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
491	| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
492	| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
493	| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
494	| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
495	| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
496	| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |
497	
498	Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
499	
500	### 14.2 Branch model
501	GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.
502	
503	| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
504	|---|---|---|
505	| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
506	| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
507	| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
508	| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
509	| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
510	| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |
511	
512	Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.
513	
514	### 14.3 CI workflows
515	
516	**QA workflow (`qa.yml`)** — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:
517	- Unit tests (Vitest)
518	- Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)
519	
520	**SIT gate (`digital-sit.yml`)** — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:
521	- Playwright `p0` priority specs
522	- Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
523	- Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
524	- Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
525	- Trend gate against the LHCI history server
526	
527	### 14.4 Deployment
528	Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:
529	
530	- **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
531	- **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
532	- **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
533	- **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
534	- **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions
535	
536	Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.
537	
538	MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.

# Technical Solution Design — Zimmermann SFCC PWA (Architecture)

*Draft for client sign-off. Last updated 2026-06-26. Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet.*

---

## 1. Purpose & Scope

This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.

**In scope:**
- Stack and build pipeline
- The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
- Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 7 storefronts in 6 regions
- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
- SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
- Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
- Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
- Open decisions requiring client input before build

**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

---

## 2. Solution Overview

A single PWA Kit codebase serves 7 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

```

                         │        Customer browser:        │
                         │ SSR'd HTML + hydrated React PWA │
                         └────────────────┬────────────────┘
                                          │
            ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
            │                             │                                 │
   CDN (Akamai / SFCC default)   Third-party SaaS APIs             (browser handoff
            │                    (browser-direct; no SFCC           at checkout for

            │                                                       ─────────────
   PWA Kit (Managed Runtime)       • Contentful                       Global-e
   React 18, SSR + CSR             • Didomi (CMP)                    (international

       (→ Google siteverify)

            │ │

                  │                         NewStore  AP21    Omneo   Narvar
                  ▼                           OMS   (loyalty  (CRM→   (EDD,

Legend / boundaries:
- **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT), Adyen Drop-In:** browser-direct from the PWA. No SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, and Crazy Egg load post-Didomi-consent only. The GTM container is served from an Addingwell-managed first-party subdomain (Addingwell is owned by Didomi); tags deployed *inside GTM* are proxied through Addingwell. **Inside Chat** is loaded by GTM (script injection through the Addingwell container, post-consent — HPC-039/040), not a direct PWA include. **Optimizely Web** and **Crazy Egg** are injected by the PWA (Optimizely: US-only, single snippet all environments, pre-render anti-flicker). Narvar Promise is domestic storefronts only — international EDD is provided by Global-e. Adyen Drop-In tokenises card data in the browser; the Adyen server API (`/payments`, notifications, refunds) runs in the SFCC cartridge. **Vimeo** hosts product video, embedded as a lazy iframe (facade-loaded to protect LCP); editorial-page video is Contentful by default but may also embed Vimeo (HPC-004).
- **PWA → Google Maps, GiveX balance check, MuleSoft (select direct calls), Booxi:** called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` — API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. GiveX balance check is not a direct GiveX call — GiveX is reachable only over a persistent TCP socket, so MRT proxies an HTTPS request to MuleSoft, which owns the GiveX connection and credentials. Boutique appointment history (CRM-165–167) is read by a PWA-direct call from the MRT Node layer straight to Booxi — SFCC and MuleSoft are not in this path. Booxi credentials held as MRT environment variables.
- **PWA → SFCC:** all commerce data (catalogue, cart, pricing, customer, orders) via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.
- **SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore / AP21 / Omneo / Narvar:** write and sync flows (order creation, fulfilment, CRM sync, EDD) — initiated by SFCC.
- **AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (inbound):** product and pricing master feed populates the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks the PWA then reads via SCAPI.
- **Omneo iFrame (My Account):** Omneo is also surfaced as a browser-direct iFrame in My Account (CRM-176), loaded with a customer-scoped session token issued server-side. All other Omneo traffic flows via MuleSoft.
- **PWA (MRT) → MuleSoft → NewStore:** read flows initiated directly by the PWA via MRT proxy — order history (CRM-056–057), order details (CRM-071–072), boutique stock check / Find in Boutique / Collect in Boutique (CFD-043). SFCC is not in this path. The channel authenticates via `client_id` + `client_secret`; `customer_id` is passed as a plain UUID query parameter.
- **SFCC server-side integrations (cartridge-based unless noted):** Avalara tax, Adyen server API (`/payments` and notifications) via cartridge; GiveX validate/redeem/refund via the **NewStore adapter** (SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adapter → GiveX), and GiveX issuance at purchase via SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX.
- **Global-e (two surfaces):** (1) **browser handoff at checkout** — the PWA routes international shipping destinations to a Zimmermann checkout page that embeds the Global-e hosted checkout in an iframe from both mini-bag and cart, with an SFCC-prepared payload; the shopper stays on `zimmermann.com` (PAY-054). Global-e owns the entire checkout, addresses, payment, duties, tax, and order confirmation email. (2) **server-side feed into SFCC** — nightly FX rates / coefficients / rounding rules from Global-e generate Global-e-market pricebooks in SFCC (PRC-34..43); a daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue CSV is pushed via SFTP (PRC-54); GiveX validate/redeem/refund webhooks are exposed to Global-e (PRC-44).

---

## 3. Frontend Stack

### 3.1 Bundled by PWA Kit
| Layer | Library | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Base framework | PWA Kit on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 | Current baseline |
| UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme tokens |
| Routing | React Router v6 | |
| Server / async state | TanStack Query via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` | All SFCC data fetching |
| i18n | react-intl | Translations under `translations/` |
| Build / dev | Webpack 5 via `pwa-kit-dev` | |

### 3.2 Project additions
| Layer | Library | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Type safety | TypeScript strict mode | All custom code is `.ts` / `.tsx` |
| Component explorer | Storybook 8 + `@storybook/addon-a11y` | `play` functions for interaction tests |
| Unit testing | Vitest (+ `vitest-axe`) | Project-level test runner |
| E2E | Playwright (+ `axe-playwright`) | Multi-region fixtures from day one |
| Forms | react-hook-form + zod | Introduced when checkout / account work begins |
| Global UI state | Zustand | Per-request store in SSR |

---

## 4. Customisation Model

All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.

**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.

**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) live in a dedicated `custom/` folder under `overrides/app/components/`, separating Zimmermann-authored components from base-template overrides at a glance.

### 4.1 Environment Configuration

All secrets and per-tier identifiers are injected as **Managed Runtime environment variables**. They must never be committed to source control or exposed in client-side bundles. The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. This TSD does not duplicate the full list (it would drift); the table below indexes the groups so each credential's boundary is clear.

| Group | Purpose | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `COMMERCE_API_*`, `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` | SFCC SCAPI / SLAS client config | Browser-direct (public client ID) + MRT-mediated (token refresh) |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` | Google Maps Places API (address autocomplete) | MRT-mediated — key never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Contentful Delivery API (published content) | Browser + SSR. CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_HOST` | Contentful Preview API (drafts, editor sessions) | MRT-mediated — proxied server-side; never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Contentful Management API (schema sync) | **Local / CI only** — never deployed to MRT |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Shared secret for the Contentful → MRT cache-purge webhook (HMAC verification) | MRT-mediated |
| `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | PWA → MuleSoft direct calls (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`): order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock, GiveX balance | MRT-mediated — credentials never reach the browser |
| `ADYEN_CLIENT_KEY`, `ADYEN_ENVIRONMENT` | Adyen Drop-In / Components SDK at checkout (tokenisation, 3DS2 inline). Server-side `/payments` calls and HMAC live in SFCC BM | Browser-direct — client key is public by design (PAY-021) |
| `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` | Inside Chat support widget. **Likely NOT PWA-owned** — Inside Chat loads via GTM script injection through the Addingwell container (HPC-039/040), so its token sits inside the GTM container config (Tell No Lies), not a PWA env var. Retain only if the PWA must initialise the widget itself; confirm with Tell No Lies | Browser-direct — public token (if used at all) |
| `NARVAR_ACCOUNT_ID` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD widget at checkout (domestic only) | Browser-direct — public ID |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 site key (registration / login forms) | Browser-direct — public site key only |
| `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 secret key — used by the MRT layer to verify tokens against Google's `siteverify` endpoint; never reaches the browser | MRT-mediated |
| `GLOBALE_*` | Global-e merchant ID, environment, script host, supported countries, server-side API key | Browser-direct (script host, merchant ID) + MRT-mediated (API key, if used) — final shape pending PRC-34..43 sign-off |
| `DIDOMI_API_KEY` | Didomi Notice/Consent ID | Browser-direct — public ID, safe in bundle |
| `GTM_CONTAINER_ID`, `GTM_SERVER_URL` | GTM container and Addingwell first-party tagging-server hostname (`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com`). The loader uses both: `${GTM_SERVER_URL}/gtm.js?id=${GTM_CONTAINER_ID}` | Browser-direct — both public, safe in bundle. One pair per environment |
| `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY`, `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` | Observability | MRT-mediated (license keys held server-side); `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (one of `local`, `dev`, `sit`, `stage`, `uat`, `prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry / New Relic / GTM |
| `MARKETING_CLOUD_*`, `COMMERCE_AGENT_SETTINGS`, `OTP_TOKEN_LENGTH` | PWA Kit base-template defaults referenced by the base runtime configuration | Likely removable once email/auth wiring is finalised (Zimmermann uses Emarsys via Omneo, not Marketing Cloud) |

**Security policy:**
- Real values live only in the local, untracked environment file; only a template — variable names, no secret values — is committed to source control.
- Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
- Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
- MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

---

## 5. Multi-Site, Multi-Locale Architecture

### 5.1 Storefronts
**7 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions**, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods. 11 active locales total. The US is a single SFCC site with checkout branching by shipping address (REG-005). EU domestic and EU international are configured as separate SFCC sites (REG-006).

| Locale | URL prefix | Currency | Checkout owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| AU + Oceania | `/` (x-default hreflang) | AUD | SFCC (REG-003) |
| UK | `/uk/` | GBP | SFCC (REG-004) |
| US (single site) | `/us/` (domestic) + `/en-ca/` (international) | USD | SFCC for US shipping; Global-e for international shipping (REG-005) |
| EU domestic — EN / FR / IT / ES | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR | SFCC (REG-006 dom) |
| EU international | `/en-ch/` | EUR | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK | `/hk/` | HKD (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-007) |
| ME | `/en-ae/` | AED (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-008) |

Rest-of-world traffic routes via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` (DMU-013). AU is configured at the root with no locale prefix and serves as the x-default hreflang target (DMU-016).

### 5.2 Entry routing
- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
- **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.

### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale
Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.

### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed
- **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
- **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
- **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
- **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.

### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts
All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

- **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
- **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
- **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

---

## 6. Checkout Ownership Branching

Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.

- **SFCC owns:** AU domestic (including Oceania — Avalara for NZ + New Caledonia), UK, US (when shipping to US), EU domestic.
- **Global-e owns:** HK, ME, EU international, the US site when shipping outside the US, and any domestic storefront when the selected shipping destination is outside that storefront's market.
- **Pricing for Global-e markets (REG-041):** SFCC holds all pricebooks (including Global-e ones), derived nightly from AP21 base prices and Global-e FX/coefficients. SFCC sends the complete cart in target currency at handoff; Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from that point. Full mechanism specified under PRC-34..43.
- **Global-e shipping country lock (REG-028):** locked at the country selector pre-checkout; cannot change once inside Global-e.

---

## 7. Integration Map

### 7.1 Classification model
Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.

- **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
- **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
- **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
- **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
- **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).

A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.

> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

### 7.2 Integration map

| System | Role | Call origin | Hosting layer | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)
All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type
PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.

| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang
Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots
Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data
Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:
- **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
- **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
- **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
- **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy
- Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
- Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
- 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)
No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

## 9. Performance Strategy

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric | Target |
|---|---|
| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule
Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags including the Inside Chat widget, via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers
- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
  - **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  - Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
- Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
- Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured
The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

## 12. Graceful Degradation

Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.

| System | Failure mode |
|---|---|
| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |
| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |
| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |

### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment

The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.

#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)

- **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
- **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.

#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)

`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sfcc-scapi` | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com` | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com` | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
| `google-places` | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD — confirm with Integration team) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |

**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).

---

## 13. Testing Strategy

Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.

| Layer | Tool | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |
| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |

### 13.1 What is tested
Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.

### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow
Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.

### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures
E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 7 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)

### 13.4 Selector priority
Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.

---

## 14. CI/CD & Environments

This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.

### 14.1 Topology

A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model
GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
|---|---|---|
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (`qa.yml`)** — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:
- Unit tests (Vitest)
- Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (`digital-sit.yml`)** — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:
- Playwright `p0` priority specs
- Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
- Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
- Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
- Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment
Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

- **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
- **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
- **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
- **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
- **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.

MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.

1	## JavaScript Hoisting & Arrow Functions Quiz
2	
3	---
4	
5	### Question 1
6	What will this code output?
7	
8	```javascript
9	greet();
10	sayHi();
11	
12	function greet() {
13	  console.log("Hello");
14	}
15	
16	var sayHi = function () {
17	  console.log("Hi");
18	};
19	```
20	
21	A. Hello / Hi  
22	B. Hello / TypeError: sayHi is not a function  
23	C. ReferenceError: sayHi is not defined  
24	D. TypeError: greet is not a function  
25	
26	Correct Answer: B  
27	Justification: Function declarations are hoisted fully, but `var sayHi` is hoisted as `undefined`, so calling it causes a TypeError.
28	
29	---
30	
31	### Question 2
32	What will happen?
33	
34	```javascript
35	console.log(a);
36	console.log(b);
37	
38	var a = 10;
39	let b = 20;
40	```
41	
42	A. undefined / 20  
43	B. 10 / 20  
44	C. undefined / ReferenceError  
45	D. ReferenceError / ReferenceError  
46	
47	Correct Answer: C  
48	Justification: `var a` is hoisted as `undefined`, but `let b` is in the Temporal Dead Zone, causing a ReferenceError.
49	
50	---
51	
52	### Question 3
53	What will this output?
54	
55	```javascript
56	const person = {
57	  name: "Alice",
58	  regular: function () {
59	    console.log(this.name);
60	  },
61	  arrow: () => {
62	    console.log(this.name);
63	  }
64	};
65	
66	person.regular();
67	person.arrow();
68	```
69	
70	A. Alice / Alice  
71	B. undefined / Alice  
72	C. Alice / undefined  
73	D. undefined / undefined  
74	
75	Correct Answer: C  
76	Justification: Regular functions bind `this` dynamically, while arrow functions inherit `this` from the outer scope.
77	
78	---
79	
80	### Question 4
81	What happens here?
82	
83	```javascript
84	multiply(2, 3);
85	
86	const multiply = (a, b) => a * b;
87	```
88	
89	A. 6  
90	B. undefined  
91	C. ReferenceError (TDZ)  
92	D. TypeError  
93	
94	Correct Answer: C  
95	Justification: Arrow functions assigned to `const` are not hoisted like function declarations and are in the Temporal Dead Zone.
96	
97	---
98	
99	### Question 5
100	What will this output?
101	
102	```javascript
103	function outer() {
104	  const arrow = () => {
105	    console.log(arguments);
106	  };
107	
108	  arrow(1, 2, 3);
109	}
110	
111	outer("a", "b");
112	```
113	
114	A. ["a", "b"]  
115	B. [1, 2, 3]  
116	C. undefined  
117	D. ReferenceError  
118	
119	Correct Answer: A  
120	Justification: Arrow functions do not have their own `arguments` object; they inherit it from `outer()`.
121	
122	---
123	
124	### Question 6
125	What will happen?
126	
127	```javascript
128	console.log(score);
129	
130	let score = 100;
131	```
132	
133	A. undefined  
134	B. 100  
135	C. ReferenceError  
136	D. TypeError  
137	
138	Correct Answer: C  
139	Justification: `let` variables are hoisted but cannot be accessed before initialization due to the Temporal Dead Zone.
140	
141	---
142	
143	### Question 7
144	What will this output?
145	
146	```javascript
147	const car = {
148	  brand: "Toyota",
149	  getBrand: () => this.brand
150	};
151	
152	console.log(car.getBrand());
153	```
154	
155	A. Toyota  
156	B. undefined  
157	C. null  
158	D. ReferenceError  
159	
160	Correct Answer: B  
161	Justification: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`, so `this.brand` is not the `car` object.
162	
163	---
164	
165	### Question 8
166	What will this output?
167	
168	```javascript
169	sayHello();
170	
171	function sayHello() {
172	  console.log("Hello!");
173	}
174	```
175	
176	A. Hello!  
177	B. undefined  
178	C. TypeError  
179	D. ReferenceError  
180	
181	Correct Answer: A  
182	Justification: Function declarations are fully hoisted, so they can be called before definition.
183	
184	---
185	
186	### Question 9
187	What will this output?
188	
189	```javascript
190	const add = (a, b) => {
191	  a + b;
192	};
193	
194	console.log(add(2, 3));
195	```
196	
197	A. 5  
198	B. undefined  
199	C. NaN  
200	D. ReferenceError  
201	
202	Correct Answer: B  
203	Justification: The function body uses `{}` without `return`, so it implicitly returns `undefined`.
204	
205	---
206	
207	### Question 10
208	What will this output?
209	
210	```javascript
211	console.log(total);
212	
213	var total = 50;
214	
215	console.log(total);
216	```
217	
218	A. undefined / 50  
219	B. 50 / 50  
220	C. ReferenceError / 50  
221	D. undefined / undefined  
222	
223	Correct Answer: A  
224	Justification: `var` is hoisted and initialized as `undefined`, then later assigned `50`.

Digital SIT Gate branches two ways: - ❌ *"Gate fails"* → back to **Developer Feature Branch** - ✅ *"Gate passes"* → **Release PR** (manual trigger, Ditigal SIT Gate re-run *(sic)*, 1x squad lead review) - In parallel, *"Auto-deploy after SIT gate"* → **OMS-INT (Parallel lane)**: NewStore SIT testing (non-blocking at Digital, blocking at Stage) 6. **Release PR** → *"Branch cut + approved"* → **Stage** (requires Digital SIT + OMS-INT — convergence point); OMS-INT also feeds Stage via *"Convergence check"* 7. **Stage** → *"Ready for UAT"* → **UAT Sign-off** (client stakeholder approval, manual gate) 8. → *"approved"* → **UAT** (client acceptance testing) 9. → *"Client sign-off"* → **Production Deploy Window** (2x squad lead approval, scheduled deployment slot) 10. → *"Deploy"* → **Production** (Salesforce MRT) --- ## Slide 14 — Scope Overview ### Platform Implementation -
